headers:
Display Message on Consent Page
(in three-legged OAuth flow)

rows.Meaning: The application will be able to read the end user’s profile data (not including associated products and services).
The application will be able to read the end user’s profile data, including associated products and services.
The application will be able to create, update, and delete the end user’s profile data, including associated products and services.
The application will only be able to read the end user’s viewable data (e.g., PNG and SVF files) within the Autodesk ecosystem.

The application will be able to read all the end user’s data (viewable and non-viewable) within the
Autodesk ecosystem.

The application will be able to create, update, and delete data on
behalf of the end user within the Autodesk ecosystem.

The application will be able to create data on behalf of the end user
within the Autodesk ecosystem.

The application will be able to search the end user’s data within
the Autodesk ecosystem.
The application will be able to create an OSS bucket it will own.

The application will be able to read the metadata and list contents
for OSS buckets that it has access to.

The application will be able to set permissions and entitlements
for OSS buckets that it has permission to modify.

The application will be able to delete a bucket that it has
permission to delete.

The application will be able to author and execute code on behalf
of the end user (e.g., scripts processed by the Design Automation
API).

rows.Display Message on Consent Page\n(in thr: View your product and service accounts
rows.Meaning:
For Product APIs, the application will be able to read the account
data the end user has entitlements to.

rows.Display Message on Consent Page\n(in thr: Manage your product and service accounts
rows.Meaning:
For Product APIs, the application will be able to update the account
data the end user has entitlements to.
The application requires this scope to generate an id_token.

data:read dynamic scope which allow
client to access the specific resource
rows.Meaning:
The application will be able to read only the resource with the URN/Object ID specified by <URN_OF_RESOURCE>.
<URN_OF_RESOURCE> takes the form urn:adsk.*. It can contain all characters (including unicode charcters) except *, \, ".

Example: urn:adsk.objects:os.object:jp-220520/box.ipt

Note: <URN_OF_RESOURCE> must be a raw URN and not a Base64 encoded URN.
